column2: Naomi asks whether she should seek rest for Ruth so that things go well with her; the negative rhetorical question and purpose clause remain.
Boaz is their acquaintance whose maidens Ruth accompanied; behold introduces his barley winnowing tonight.
column3: Winnowing barley on the threshing floor interprets the Greek winnowing the barley-floor expression by its contents and location.

column2: Washing, anointing, clothing and going up precede the prohibition on recognition until drinking and eating are finished; go up and the drink/eat order remain.
The place of his lying must be observed before approach, uncovering what is at his feet and lying down; he will then tell her what to do.
column3: What is at his feet preserves the open expression without specifying a body part, garment or sexual action.

column2: Ruth promises to do all Naomi says, keeping the scope of all and the future response.
She goes down and follows all instructions; the down movement is not altered to match the up instruction in verse 3.
Boaz eats and becomes glad, lies at part of the heap, and Ruth secretly uncovers what is at his feet; no drinking or additional lying action is inserted here.
Midnight brings both startling and disturbance, then behold reveals the woman lying at his feet; all three clauses remain.
Ruth identifies herself as his handmaid and asks his wing to cover her because he is a near kinsman; the wing image and repeated handmaid remain.
column3: Of your garment is a contextual specification of pterygion, not a separate Greek garment noun; it links the clothing setting with the broader wing image without adding a marriage ceremony.

column2: The Lord-God blessing credits her latter mercy above the former, specifically not following younger men, whether poor or rich; the comparison remains.
The assurance of action and command against fear lead into the people's knowledge that she is a woman of strength; the sentence continues to verse 12.
And that continues the knowledge construction with his kinship, followed by a nearer kinsman; the two relationships remain without dropping the selected continuation.
column3: The extent of the whole tribe's knowledge clause across the boundary remains syntactically difficult and is not presented as independently settled.

column2: The overnight stay, nearer man's first opportunity, conditional fallback, oath as the Lord lives and repeated sleep-until-morning instruction all remain.
Ruth stays at his feet until morning but rises before mutual recognition is possible; Boaz's secrecy instruction concerns a woman's arrival at the floor.
The wrap, six unspecified measures of barley, loading onto her and entry into the city remain.
column3: She held it, he measured and he entered supply contextual subjects for unexpressed Greek subjects; the final entrant is especially unresolved. Measures is a necessary English quantity head, without a supplied oiphi or other fixed unit.

column2: Ruth explicitly enters to Naomi, who asks Who are you, daughter, then hears all the man's actions; the unusual identity question is not replaced with How did it go.
Six measures are repeated with Boaz's explanation against returning empty to Naomi; empty-handed expresses empty in the gift-carrying context.
Naomi tells her to sit until she knows how the matter will not fall, because the man will certainly not rest before finishing today.
column3: The negative fall-through idiom remains selected but unresolved; it is not silently rewritten as a positive how the matter turns out. Both the time limit today and emphatic no-rest clause remain.

column2: Boaz sits at the gate and behold introduces the passing kinsman; unnamed one preserves the source's concealed-name address without inventing a personal name.
column3: Kryphie may be an anonymous-address idiom rather than a description of secrecy; unnamed one remains provisional.

column2: Ten city elders are seated as witnesses; he in English continues the explicit Boaz subject of the selected clause without ambiguity here.
The Abimelech field portion is given to returning Naomi; the English makes the Greek relative construction a statement without changing it into a sale.
column3: The legal relation between the field, Naomi and the later acquisition request requires specialist review; no Hebrew-based sale verb is inserted.

column2: Propose For before there is no one to retain hoti's explanation of priority; the uncover-your-ear image, public acquisition, two conditions and I-after-you order remain.
column3: Uncover your ear means disclose/inform in this context. I am he supplies an English complement to ego eimi in the kinsman's reply without theological implication.

column2: Acquisition is from Naomi's hand and from Ruth, the dead man's wife, and includes acquiring her herself to raise his name on the inheritance.
column3: The selected explicit necessity and Ruth's relation to acquisition remain; the legal categories are not conflated with an independently established Hebrew practice.

column2: The kinsman refuses because of feared destruction of his own inheritance, transfers his kinship right and repeats inability; the reflexive interests remain.
The former ordinance covers kinship and exchange, with sandal removal and transfer to the neighbour exercising that right as testimony in Israel.
column3: Every matter renders pan logon in the transaction context; this is the narrator's custom description, not contemporary legal guidance.

column2: The kinsman explicitly yields his right to Boaz and both removes and gives the sandal; neither act is omitted.
Elders and all people witness acquisition from Naomi of everything belonging to Abimelech, Chilion and Mahlon; the selected sons' order remains.
Ruth is identified as Mahlon's wife and acquired as Boaz's wife for the dead man's name; preservation among brothers and tribe precedes the repeated witnesses-today declaration.
People confirm witness, then elders compare the entering wife with Rachel and Leah, both builders of Israel who established strength in Ephrathah.
column3: The plural established-strength verb stays with Rachel and Leah, not a new second-person wish to Boaz; there shall be a name in Bethlehem remains without a supplied possessor.

column2: The house blessing invokes Perez born to Tamar and Judah, through seed the Lord will give from this young woman; ancestry and future gift remain.
Boaz takes Ruth as wife and goes in to her; the Lord gives conception and she bears a son, preserving the separate human and divine actions.
The women bless the Lord for not leaving Naomi without the kinsman and wish that he call your name in Israel; the selected your remains.
column3: The subject of may he call is unresolved between possible antecedents; lower-case he avoids deciding it through capitalization, and the inherited dagger note remains.

column2: The child will restore life and nourish old age because the loving daughter-in-law bore him and is better than seven sons; the seven comparison remains.
column3: Life renders psyche in the restoration context; old age renders grey hair metonymically without changing the beneficiary.

column2: Naomi takes the child to her bosom and becomes his nurse; the text is not expanded into a claim about lactation or adoption procedure.
The neighbouring women name him Obed while saying a son is born to Naomi; the narrator identifies Obed as Jesse's father and David's grandfather.
The genealogy opens with Perez and Hezron, using begot in the established Genesis cadence.
Hezron begets Arran, and Arran Amminadab; selected Arran is not normalized to Ram or Aram.
Amminadab begets Nahshon, and Nahshon Salman; selected Salman remains distinct from alternate forms elsewhere.
Salman begets Boaz, and Boaz Obed; the genealogy joins the narrative without an omitted generation.
Obed begets Jesse, and Jesse David, completing the selected ten-name chain from Perez with nine begetting links.
